subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam, and if so should the first implementation bridge to Gateway `tools.media.audio` with explicit credential, private-network, and fallback policy?
rationale: The source proves the capability is missing, but implementing it safely requires maintainer intent for native app versus Gateway/provider ownership, microphone-audio routing, SecretRef handling, network trust, fallback behavior, and overlay UX.

options.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
options.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native PTT backend abstraction that keeps Apple Speech as default and uses existing media/provider request controls for configured batch STT.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Keep native PTT on Apple Speech until the team has a broader native ASR plan across PTT, Talk, wake-word, and mobile surfaces.

options.title: Route only through external/plugin surfaces
options.body: Close or narrow the core request if maintainers decide sidecars or plugin/provider paths are sufficient and native capture should not gain a backend seam.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native PTT backend abstraction that keeps Apple Speech as default and uses existing media/provider request controls for configured batch STT.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is in native macOS voice/PTT code, while the provider-security details can be co-reviewed with media/provider owners.
